qc_a_gauche_de_l_aiguille.blurb: Gauche de l'aiguille is the left-hand side of the L'Aiguille cliff at Val-David in the Laurentians, in the Dufresne part of the regional park. It holds 18 routes, mostly traditional lines (14) with four bolted ones. A few easy leads and moderate climbs start the range at the 5.5 to 5.7 level, but the bulk of the climbing is 5.11 and 5.12, with some 5.10 between. Several lines follow cracks, and many can be top-roped once the anchors are reached. The cliff lies near the parking area and tends to draw a crowd, so expect company on good days.

qc_01_la_tache_noire.blurb: La tache noire is the first sector on the left side of L'Amphitheatre, a quartzite cliff near Saint-Andre-de-Kamouraska. It has 18 routes, twelve of them bolted leads and six set up as top-ropes, and it carries the most easy climbing of any sector on the wall. Grades run from the lower 5.x range up to 5.12, with the greatest concentration between 5.9 and 5.11. That spread makes it a reasonable first stop for newer leaders while still giving stronger climbers something to try. The cliff as a whole gets busy on weekends.

qc_b_l_aiguille.blurb: L'aiguille is a free-standing pillar of rock set apart from the main cliff at Val-David in the Laurentians, in the centre of the cliff line where it is hard to miss. Most of its 18 entries are traditional routes (15), plus three boulder problems in the V4 to V6 range. Roped grades run from an easy 5.2 chimney up to 5.12, with the heaviest cluster at 5.10 and 5.11. Routes ascend the north and west faces. Top-ropes can be rigged along both faces after first leading an easier line, and some lines need directionals.

qc_fleur_de_lys_onsite.blurb: Fleur-de-Lys is an urban boulder in Quebec City, set within the Place Jean-Beliveau park. It is a granite block placed there by OnSite, so the climbing is manufactured but on real rock. All 18 problems are boulders, spanning V3 to V10. The middle of the range is the busiest: roughly V3 through V7 account for nearly every problem, with a single V8 and one V10 project-level line at the top. Being in a city park, it suits a short session between other plans rather than a full day trip.

qc_secteur_3_me_cap.blurb: The 3eme Cap is a sector of Chikebana, also called La Grotte, near Ville-Marie in Abitibi-Temiscamingue. It has 18 routes, split between bolted leads and traditional lines, and some can be top-roped. Grades start around 5.6 and stretch to 5.12, though most sit between 5.8 and 5.10, which makes it friendly to moderate climbers. The granite faces stay in shade through the morning, holding it until about half past noon in July. Reaching the base takes roughly ten minutes on a marked trail.

qc_left_rib_aka_copacabana.blurb: Left Rib, known as Copacabana, is a steep section of Gatineau Park's old, featured granite, reached on a short trail that branches off near Down Under. It offers 18 routes, mostly sport (14) with four trad lines, on walls that top out around 20 metres. The climbing is powerful and bouldery, steeper than the neighbouring wall. There is nothing for beginners here: grades begin near 5.10, then thicken from 5.11 up through 5.12 and 5.13, with a hard 5.14 at the top end.

qc_a_secteur_de_valentin.blurb: Secteur de Valentin sits at the northern end of the canyon at Pont-Rouge, on the river's west bank, and is a winter venue for ice and mixed climbing. Its 17 routes split almost evenly between mixed lines (M6 to M8) and ice from WI4 up to WI7, so it favours experienced ice climbers rather than novices. From the top of the wooden stairs the first lines are a short walk to the right along the same side of the river. Every route can be descended by rappelling off trees. Bolts on the mixed lines blend into the rock, and eye protection is advised.

qc_b_joker.blurb: Joker is the largest of the crags in the Dame de Coeur zone above Val-David, reached on the marked trail in. It has 17 routes, mostly bolted (13) with four trad lines, on high-friction anorthosite. The wall faces southwest, so it takes sun from mid-morning right through the afternoon and the base has no shade. That makes it good in spring and fall but punishing in midsummer heat. Grades start around 5.7 and run up into the 5.12 and low 5.13 range. The far right end is known for unusual wave-like rock shapes.
